q: Why are thylakoids described as a 'system' for the light-dependent reactions?
options: Each thylakoid carries out both the light-dependent reactions and the Calvin cycle on its own
Photosystems, carriers and ATP synthase work together in one membrane to make ATP, NADPH and O2
Thylakoids are free-floating pigment molecules that collide randomly to pass energy between them
Thylakoids store the glucose produced by the light-dependent reactions until the cell needs it later
explanation: A system is a set of interacting parts with properties none has alone. In the thylakoid membrane, PSII (photolysis), plastoquinone, cytochrome b6f, plastocyanin, PSI, ferredoxin/NADP reductase and ATP synthase are positioned precisely. The membrane separates the lumen from the stroma, allowing a proton gradient, and the products (ATP, NADPH) are released into the stroma for the Calvin cycle.
